The dark default window (S01) and Hide UI (S06) match Figma except for one undocumented seek-head offset, the documented macOS traffic lights (D007/D022), and the light screen (S72), which needs a closer fixture and a note on the divider. summary:
Read-only parity judgement for the control bar and seek bar group, on claude/final at 4c457baa03 plus the area agents' uncommitted edits. I reran check for every entry with a Figma node, rendered the 15 entries without one, and compared the crops by eye against the Figma renders and the video key frames. Nothing in the group is a major difference. The controls match pixel for pixel: play/pause, time labels, seek track, fill and head, the volume cone at 0–200 % (dark and light), the volume tooltip, the seek preview card, the resume toast and marker, the subtitle-timeline styling and the music waveform bar. The remaining FAIL verdicts come from these sources:
(1) The playhead sits about 13.5 pt right of Figma's because the fixture uses the real 130/1540 ratio. This is recorded only as a gallery note, not as a DECISIONS line or figmaDeviation. It affects C.SeekBar/default, S01.ControlBar/default, S01.Window/shipping and S34.ControlBar/music.
(2) S21.Timeline differs because Figma leaves an 18 pt gap between fill and head. The video has no gap and the product follows the video, but this is not recorded.
(3) Component 491:1779 has a 1 pt top stroke that Player-6 does not, and the product follows Player-6 (audit PLAYER-05). This is not in DECISIONS.
Real differences to fix (all minor, owner B-controls unless noted):
(a) Bar icons brighten to FG/1 on hover, but Figma 177:99 keeps FG/A2 and only adds the 6 % white tile (PlayerControls.swift:43).
(b) The seek preview is offset by the frame's internal 10 pt gap. It overlaps the control bar by about 3 pt, while the video shows it about 18 pt above the track, clear of the bar (PlayerControls.swift:441).
(c) A live stream shows a duration of \"00:00:00\" with the head at 0.
(d) The OSD shadow is much weaker than the video's crisp dark edge. D027 covers the font itself.
(e) H-design: the light play button uses the Light/Accent token #E8851A, while the Player - Light frame uses #D37918.
Documented and therefore not counted: the waveform is off by default (D028), which is why the music app shows a solid bar; proportional digits (D047); the light bar tint (D046); and the narrow resume toast, which keeps only the button and close.
Owner decisions are untouched. The D041 pause pin affects only bar visibility while paused.
Live checks to run on an idle Mac:
- Seek preview position and follow-on-drag, and the paused-seek still (D031/D047).
- Tooltip position and wheel direction.
- Pressed states: neither Figma nor the video defines one, and the product has none.
- OSD readability over a bright frame.
- Bar reveal and hide timing, and cursor hiding in fullscreen.
- Compact overflow behaviour while resizing.
All outputs are under <scratch> check/<entry>/ holds render, ref and diff-heatmap images; r/ holds the renders; stack1-3.png, cmp_*.png, light_bar.png, live_bar.png and kf_*.png are the side-by-side images.

I judged the side-panel group (S14–S24, the metadata overlay, presets and filter cards) on claude/final at HEAD 4c457baa03 plus the uncommitted edits. I compared each panel with its Figma render and the video key frames, side by side. Outputs are in <scratch> (check/<entry>/ for the Figma checks, win/ for the full-window renders).

**One real major gap: the expanded filter cards (S18 and S19).** The shared expand component (Sources/MXRUI/Panels/PanelControls.swift, the `PanelExpand` struct) keeps the dark "Expand Settings" bar when the card is open. It only changes the label to "Collapse Settings" and the chevron to up, and puts the rows underneath with nothing around them. Figma (Video - Essential, Audio - Compressor Settings) and the video (08m49) show something else when a card is open: one lighter card that holds the "Collapse Settings" header with a down chevron and all the sliders. In Figma's Essential card each slider has only a label above it; in the Compressor card the value sits as text on the right. Instead, our rows are a label plus a value field, with the slider below. Video's Essential/Crop/Colors and Audio's EQ/Compressor/Spatializer/Stereo Widener all look like this. No gallery entry shows an open card next to its Figma frame, so the Figma checks never catch it. Owner: G-panels.

**Everything else matches or is covered by a decision.**
- The Playback tab FAIL is entirely the D033 row list (Show Waveform and Show Metadata instead of Show Statistics) plus D014 (Reverse turned off, with an ⓘ). It matches video frame 09m17.5.

**Waiting on the owner:** the Relative font-size slider puts Auto at stop 0, while Figma's thumb is at stop 3 (D033). The Appearance render follows the current implementation.

**Infrastructure (I did not edit anything outside my folder):**
1. **The disk is almost full.** The data volume had 318 MB free; I deleted my own 341 MB scratch build and it now has about 720 MB. Other agents' `swift build` runs will start failing with "no space left on device" (ENOSPC). The biggest scratch folders are F-settings-verify-r2 and integration, about 650 MB each.
2. **Tool bug in `mxr-snapshot`.** `GalleryPaths.locate()` in Sources/MXRGalleryCatalog/GalleryCatalog.swift loops forever, using full CPU, when it runs from a package copy outside the repo and `MXR_REPO_ROOT` is not set: going up from "/" never gives back "/". Setting `MXR_REPO_ROOT` avoids it.

The cone icon's only layer is styled as an accent layer, and `MXRIcon` paints that with `accentMain`. The `tint: Theme.Color.accentLogo` passed in `PlayerBars.swift:236`, `PlayerView.swift:57` and `MediaInfoDialogs.swift:76` is ignored. Dark is unaffected because the two colours are equal there.

   - The onboarding shortcuts footer sits about 1 pt lower.
